deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp.4-6): Grothendieck studies outer automorphisms of the profinite 'groupe à lacets' π̂_{0,3}, the fundamental group of P^1 minus {0,1,∞} with its loop (inertia) structure. It is generated by l_0, l_1, l_∞ with l_0 l_1 l_∞ = 1. On p.4 he defines the 3-cycle ρ (l_0→l_1→l_∞→l_0) and the involution σ_∞ (swaps l_0 and l_1, sends l_∞ to l_0^{-1}l_1^{-1}). He obtains σ_0 and σ_1 by ρ-conjugation, ρσ_iρ^{-1} = σ_{ρ(i)}. Explicitly:
- σ_0: l_1↔l_∞, l_0 ↦ l_1^{-1}l_∞^{-1}.
- σ_1: l_0↔l_∞, l_1 ↦ l_∞^{-1}l_0^{-1}.
Each σ_i is a genuine involution and ρ^3 = id, so Z/3 = ⟨ρ⟩ acts genuinely on π.

On this page he shows that the S_3 relations hold only up to inner automorphisms. In S_3 one has σ_0σ_1 = σ_1σ_∞ = σ_∞σ_0 = ρ. In Aut(π) he computes σ_0σ_1:
- l_0 ↦ l_1.
- l_1 ↦ l_1^{-1}l_∞l_1.
- l_∞ ↦ l_1^{-1}l_∞^{-1} = l_1^{-1}l_0l_1.
Hence σ_0σ_1 = int(l_1^{-1})ρ, and by ρ-symmetry σ_1σ_∞ = int(l_∞^{-1})ρ and σ_∞σ_0 = int(l_0^{-1})ρ. So one gets a homomorphism S_3 → Out(π) respecting the loop structure (multiplier 1), but not the given lift to Aut(π).

He then argues that no genuine action of S_3 on the discrete π can realise this outer action. The reason is that S_3 acts on P^1−{0,1,∞} without a common fixed point. Modern justification: since π has trivial centre, the outer action defines a unique extension. Topologically this extension is the orbifold group of [X/S_3], namely PSL_2(Z) ⊃ Γ(2) with quotient S_3. Lifts to Aut correspond to splittings, and by realisation of finite subgroups as stabilisers, a splitting would need a point with stabiliser S_3. Equivalently, PSL_2(Z) = Z/2*Z/3 has no S_3 subgroup.

By contrast Z/3 does act genuinely, because ρ (z ↦ 1/(1−z)) has fixed points, which can serve as base point for π_1.

Finally he announces complex conjugation τ in the extended Teichmüller group Γ_{0,3}. On the next page this gives Γ_{0,3} = S_3 × {±1} acting outer-ly on π_{0,3}, followed by the study of outer automorphisms commuting with τ, normalised by u(l_0) = l_0^{χ(u)}. These are the first steps toward the Ihara/Drinfeld-type description of the Galois / Grothendieck–Teichmüller action on π̂_{0,3}.
errors: Fixed points of the 3-cycle z ↦ 1/(1−z) on P^1−{0,1,∞} are the roots of z^2−z+1 = 0, i.e. −j and −j^2 = e^{±iπ/3}. These are primitive SIXTH roots of unity, not primitive cube roots as the marginal note says ('±j (racines primitives troisièmes de 1)'). Minor slip.

Statement 'S_3 opère sans point fixe' should read 'without common (global) fixed point': each transposition does have fixed points (1/2, −1, 2). The argument implicitly uses this weaker, correct statement.
All group-theoretic computations on the page check out (σ_0σ_1 = int(l_1^{-1})ρ etc., with int(g)(x) = gxg^{-1}).

ideas.what: Outer action of S_3 (permuting 0,1,∞) on the loop group π_{0,3}, given by explicit automorphisms ρ, σ_i whose S_3 relations hold only modulo inner automorphisms
ideas.modern_name: S_3 symmetry of P^1−{0,1,∞}; outer action of PGL_2(Z)/Γ(2) on the free group F_2; precursor of the 2-cycle and 3-cycle relations in Ihara/Drinfeld's GT
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Fricke–Klein symmetries); in the GT context Drinfeld 1990 and Ihara 1990s
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984), discussion of Γ_{0,3}, Γ_{0,4} and the Teichmüller tower, in less explicit form

ideas.what: Non-realisability of the S_3 outer action by a genuine action on the discrete group, because S_3 has no common fixed point; Z/3 lifts because it has a fixed point
ideas.modern_name: Non-splitting of 1→Γ(2)/±1→PSL_2(Z)→S_3→1; finite subgroups of orbifold groups are stabilisers (Nielsen realisation)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Kerékjártó, Nielsen; free-product structure of PSL_2(Z))

ideas.what: Extended Teichmüller group Γ_{0,3} = S_3 × {±1} including complex conjugation τ acting on π_{0,3} (next page)
ideas.modern_name: Extended mapping class group of the thrice-punctured sphere
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (Teichmüller tower, Γ_{g,ν} including orientation reversal)

missed.claim: Grothendieck pins down explicitly (1981) the inner-automorphism defect of the S_3 action on π_{0,3}, σ_0σ_1 = int(l_1^{-1})ρ, as the start of describing outer automorphisms of π̂_{0,3} compatible with the S_3 × {±1} action. This is exactly the bookkeeping behind Drinfeld's (1990) GT relations f(x,y)f(y,x) = 1 and the 3-cycle relation, and Ihara's normalisation. It is historically noteworthy as a precursor but mathematically routine.
missed.quote: donc σ_0σ_1 = int(ℓ_1^{-1})ρ dans Aut(π) ... On a une représentation de S_3 dans le groupe extérieur à lacets seulement.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Documents that Grothendieck was computing the S_3/τ-symmetry constraints on Gal(Q̄/Q) → Out(π̂_{0,3}) in 1981, nearly a decade before GT. This is of historical interest only; there is no new mathematics.

deep.surprise_reason: Correct but routine computation of the S_3 outer action on the free group of rank 2, plus the standard fixed-point obstruction to lifting. Its only interest is historical, as an early explicit step toward GT-type symmetry relations, which are already associated with Grothendieck's Esquisse programme.
transcription_corrections: First line: 'par ρ, mais pas de 𝔖_3, car ... p.ex' (i.e. not of all of S_3).
Crossed-out line reads roughly '[σ_0,σ_1] ... = (σ_0σ_1)^2 = ρ^2', which is fine as given.
Marginal note '±j (racines primitives troisièmes de 1)' is faithfully transcribed but mathematically should be −j, −j^2 (primitive sixth roots of unity).
'groupe de Teichmüller élargi' is a plausible reading of the last lines, with the insertion 'Γ_{0,3} opérant sur π_{0,3}'.
'qu'on peut prendre comme origine pour calculer le π_1' (rather than 'pris').
